notes: Actual results for calendar year 2025, as the city reported them in its annual financial report to the Ohio Auditor of State (unaudited). Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Madison County and, unless the municipality has left it, the surrounding township.
Most Ohio cities and villages levy a municipal income tax, which is counted with other local taxes.

Governmental funds are reported by function. Capital outlay has no function, so it is spread over the other spending in proportion. Utility funds count operating revenue and expenses (depreciation left out) plus nonoperating revenue and debt payments.

Intergovernmental disbursements, payments to refunded bond escrow agents, borrowing, transfers, advances, sales of capital assets and special or extraordinary items are left out. Debt service also leaves out $698,195 of principal repaid with new borrowing the city did not spend on capital that year, most likely notes rolled over.
General government, courts, community and economic development and community environment count as overhead.
Debt is long-term obligations at year end (bonds, notes, loans and leases), as reported.
Political money is not scored: Ohio local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county board of elections, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 7 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of London's borders in OpenStreetMap (7 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Ohio yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 7 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of London's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

notes: Actual results for calendar year 2025, as the village reported them in its annual financial report to the Ohio Auditor of State (unaudited). Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Madison County and, unless the municipality has left it, the surrounding township.
Most Ohio cities and villages levy a municipal income tax, which is counted with other local taxes.

Governmental funds are reported by function. Capital outlay has no function, so it is spread over the other spending in proportion. Utility funds count operating revenue and expenses (depreciation left out) plus nonoperating revenue and debt payments.

Intergovernmental disbursements, payments to refunded bond escrow agents, borrowing, transfers, advances, sales of capital assets and special or extraordinary items are left out. Debt service also leaves out $128,492 of principal repaid with new borrowing the village did not spend on capital that year, most likely notes rolled over.
General government, courts, community and economic development and community environment count as overhead.
Debt is long-term obligations at year end (bonds, notes, loans and leases), as reported.
Political money is not scored: Ohio local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county board of elections, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 3 license-plate cameras are mapped inside Village of Plain City's borders in OpenStreetMap (3 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Ohio yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 3 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside Village of Plain City's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
